       43 +                                                              
       44 +### 2. The retransmission / forwarding path — established from
          + the code, then verified byte by byte                         
       45 +- The semantics were **derived from the production code**, not
          + invented:                                                    
       46 +  `ProcessorRxVideo::checkAndRequestMissingPackets()` builds a
       47 +  `PACKET_TYPE_VIDEO_REQ_MULTIPLE_PACKETS` request (retransmis
          +sion id, video                                                
       48 +  stream index, flags, count, (block index, packet index) pair
          +s) and queues it                                              
       49 +  in the high priority queue; the vehicle answers with the mis
          +sing video                                                    
       50 +  packets marked with `PACKET_FLAGS_BIT_RETRANSMITED` +       
       51 +  `PACKET_FLAGS_BIT_HIGH_PRIORITY` and the retransmission id i
          +n the video                                                   
       52 +  stream info (`code/r_vehicle/video_tx_buffers.cpp: _sendPack
          +et()`).                                                       
       53 +- Two things had to be got right, and both were found by the f
          +ailures:                                                      
       54 +  - The **frame packet index convention**: the low byte of `uF
          +ramePacketsInfo`                                              
       55 +    is the index of the packet **inside the frame, counted for
          +ward** (the                                                   
       56 +    vehicle counts the packets of the frame from the end and d
          +ecrements while                                               
       57 +    it walks the frame backwards). With the wrong convention t
          +he station                                                    
       58 +    believes that the end of the frame is missing.            
       59 +  - The **retransmission window**: with the retransmissions di
          +sabled (or with                                               
       60 +    the window bits unset) the model computes a window of 0 ms
          + and                                                          
       61 +    `checkAndDiscardBlocksTooOld()` throws the just-received b
          +lock away before                                              
       62 +    the request is built ("Discarded 2 blocks too old"). The t
          +est therefore                                                 
       63 +    enables `VIDEO_PROFILE_ENCODING_FLAG_ENABLE_RETRANSMISSION
          +S` with                                                       
       64 +    `DEFAULT_VIDEO_RETRANS_MS5_HP` (70 ms), the way the models
          + do.                                                          
       65 +- **Test 13** (new): the request is built and every field is c
          +hecked (36                                                    
       66 +  bytes, the type, the component, the high priority flag, the 
          +destination                                                   
       67 +  vehicle, a non-zero retransmission id, the stream index, the
          + flags, the                                                   
       68 +  count, the block index and the packet index). The second req
          +uest for the                                                  
       69 +  same missing packet carries the "re-requested" flag (0x01) a
          +nd a **new**                                                  
       70 +  retransmission id.                                          
       71 +- **Test 14** (new): the request is put on the air with the pr
          +oduction TX                                                   
       72 +  builder — the bytes on the air are the bytes of the request,
          + except the CRC                                               
       73 +  (offsets 0-3) and the radio link index (offsets 14-15), and 
          +the CRC of the                                                
       74 +  on-air packet is valid. The answer of the VTX is built and m
          +arked exactly                                                 
       75 +  as the vehicle side marks it; the station accepts it, comple
          +tes the block and                                             
       76 +  delivers the **whole 9576-byte frame** to the desktop player
          +'s FIFO, with                                                 
       77 +  the retransmitted packet counted as retransmitted and **not*
          +* discarded.                                                  
       78 +- Two test-only seams were needed because the real ones live i
          +n                                                             
       79 +  `ruby_rt_station.cpp`, next to its `main()`: `router_get_las
          +t_time_checked_for_video_packets()`                           
       80 +  and `router_is_eof()` (they are only used for the log messag
          +es of the                                                     
       81 +  requests). No production code was changed for them.         
       82 +                                                              
       83 +### 3. A real defect in the RX block buffer — found by the new
          + tests                                                        
       84 +`code/r_station/video_rx_buffers.cpp` validated the video data
          + length of                                                    
       85 +**every** packet of a block, including the EC packets. On an E
          +C packet the                                                  
       86 +video data area holds the **FEC parity block**: the vehicle wr
          +ites the parity                                               
       87 +over the important header, so `uVideoDataLength` there is pari
          +ty garbage and                                                
       88 +not a length. The check read that garbage, rejected the valid 
          +EC packets and                                                
       89 +the blocks were never completed (4 EC reconstruction tests fai
          +led).                                                         
       90 +*Fix*: the length check is applied to the data packets only, a
          +nd the EC                                                     
       91 +packets have their own minimum-length check (the parity block 
          +must fit in the                                               
       92 +packet). The EC reconstruction tests are green again.         
       93 +                                                              
       94 +### 4. Live video in the desktop application — demonstrated   
       95 +- **New** `--live-feed` mode of `test_video_rx_pipeline`: it s
          +ends the real                                                 
       96 +  H.264 stream (`res/intro.h264`, 896970 bytes, 150 access uni
          +ts) through the                                               
       97 +  **production** receive path in real time, at the frame rate 
          +of the clip                                                   
       98 +  (15 fps), exactly as the radio RX thread would:             
       99 +  `process_received_video_component_packet()` → `ProcessorRxVi
          +deo` →                                                        
      100 +  `VideoRxPacketsBuffer` → `rx_video_output_video_data()` → th
          +e FIFO                                                        
      101 +  `/tmp/ruby/fifovideo_disp`. The packets are built the way th
          +e vehicle                                                     
      102 +  builds them (the same headers, the same CRC, the same block 
          +scheme, the                                                   
      103 +  forward frame packet index).                                
      104 +  The only difference from the other test cases is the FIFO: i
          +n the live feed                                               
      105 +  the FIFO is read by the **desktop player**, not by the test 
          +(two readers of                                               
      106 +  a FIFO split the stream between them), so the test does not 
          +open the read                                                 
      107 +  end. The FIFO is created only if it is not already there, so
          + a player that                                                
      108 +  has it open is not left reading from a deleted FIFO.        
      109 +- *Verified on this machine* (the user was warned with a deskt
          +op notification                                               
      110 +  before the screen was taken over, the window was restored af
          +terwards):                                                    
      111 +  - the player logged "Received the first video stream data" a

      112 +    format (`video/x-raw NV12 1280x720`);                     
      113 +  - the station detected the stream: "Detected video stream FP

      114 +    "Detected H264 stream level: 41 (0x29)";                  
      115 +  - the player read **10.85 MB** from the FIFO in 120 s of str
          +eaming;                                                       
      116 +  - the decoded video was **rendered on screen**: the screensh
          +ots of the

          +o and the

      399 +---                                                           
      400 +                                                              
      401 +## 7. A monitor-mode-capable adapter (Q1): what the adapter mu
          +st do, and which ones do                                      
      402 +                                                              
      403 +**First, the exact requirement.** A chipset name is not enough
          +: an adapter is                                               
      404 +usable for the RubyFPV 802.11 video path only if it does **all
          +** of these:                                                  
      405 +                                                              
      406 +1. **Monitor mode.** The RX path is pcap based: `radio_open_in
          +terface_for_read()`                                           
      407 +   opens a pcap handle on the interface and installs the filte
          +r                                                             
      408 +   `radio[0x40:2] == 0x0801 && radio[0x4a:4] == 0x13123456 && 
          +...`                                                          
      409 +   (`code/radio/radiolink.c`). Without `NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR
          +` there is no                                                 
      410 +   capture of the raw 802.11 frames.                          
      411 +2. **The raw frame, with the radiotap header.** The code parse
          +s the received                                                
      412 +   frame with `ieee80211_radiotap_iterator_init()` and it need
          +s the link type                                               
      413 +   `DLT_IEEE802_11_RADIOTAP`. An adapter in "managed" mode (Et
          +hernet                                                        
      414 +   encapsulation) is useless.                                 
      415 +3. **Injection on a monitor interface.** The TX path is `pcap_
          +inject()` of a                                                
      416 +   radiotap + 802.11 frame (`radio_write_raw_ieee_packet()`), 
          +so the adapter                                                
      417 +   must accept injected frames and put them on the air at the 
          +requested rate                                                
      418 +   (RubyFPV sends with the legacy radiotap header or with the 
          +MCS one).                                                     
      419 +4. **A fixed channel in the 5.8 GHz band.** The video link of 
          +the models is                                                 
      420 +   5.8 GHz and the card must be able to stay on one channel wh
          +ile it is in                                                  
      421 +   monitor mode (the injection of some drivers breaks if the c
          +hannel is                                                     
      422 +   changed or if the card is scanning).                       
      423 +5. **5.8 GHz in hardware.** The antennas of the card must cove
          +r                                                             
      424 +   5.725–5.850 GHz. The card that is on this machine (`Eachine
          + WiFiLink`,                                                   
      425 +   RTL8812AU) has **5 GHz-only antennas** and that is why the 
          +software guard                                                
      426 +   `radio_cap_card_model_is_5ghz_only()` (model 7) refuses to 
          +tune it to                                                    
      427 +   2.4 GHz. That guard must not be weakened.                  
      428 +6. **Enough USB bandwidth.** The video stream is 2–4 Mbps; a U
          +SB 2.0 link is                                                
      429 +   enough.                                                    
      430 +7. **A USB id that RubyFPV knows.** The card model is detected
          + from the USB                                                 
      431 +   product id (`code/base/hardware_radio.c`), and the model se
          +lects the                                                     
      432 +   antenna guard and the TX power table (`code/base/tx_powers.
          +cpp`). A new                                                  
      433 +   adapter needs a small entry there — a code change, not a dr
          +iver change.                                                  
      434 +                                                              
      435 +**Second, the candidates, with the evidence.**                
      436 +                                                              
      437 +| Adapter / chipset | USB id | Driver (in-tree) | Bands | Moni
          +tor | Injection | Active monitor | Verdict for RubyFPV |      
      438 +|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|                             
      439 +| **ALFA AWUS036ACM** / MT7612U | 0e0d:7612 | `mt76x2u` (mt76)
          + | 2.4 + 5 | yes | yes, at all MCS levels | yes | **the best c
          +andidate**: 5 GHz, in-tree, injection verified |              
      440 +| **ALFA AWUS036ACHM** / MT7610U | 0e0d:7606 | `mt76x0u` (mt76
          +) | 2.4 + 5 | yes | yes | yes | also good, and the cheapest | 
      441 +| Panda PAU0B (MT7610U), ASUS USB-AC51 (MT7610U) | 0e0d:7606 |
          + `mt76x0u` | 2.4 + 5 | yes | yes | yes | the same chipset, che
          +aper |                                                        
      442 +| AR9271 | 0cf3:9271 | `ath9k_htc` | **2.4 only** | yes | yes 
          +(but it ignores the radiotap TX flags) | no | 2.4 GHz only → i
          +t would need a 2.4 GHz model and a different antenna; not the 
          +reference band |                                              
      443 +| RT3572 / RT2800U | 148f:3572 | `rt2800usb` | **2.4 only** | 
          +yes | yes | no | same limitation as the AR9271 |              
      444 +| ALFA AWUS036AXM / MT7921U | 0e0d:7921 | `mt7921u` | 2.4 + 5 
          ++ 6 | **broken** (as of kernel 6.18) | injects at 1 Mbps (2.4)
          + / 6 Mbps (5) | no | **not recommended** |                    
      445 +| Netgear A9000 / MT7925U | 7925? | `mt7925u` | 2.4 + 5 + 6 | 
          +yes (verified end of 2025) | yes | yes | good, but WiFi 7 and 
          +the newest, so the least proven |                             
      446 +| The **existing** RTL8812AU (`wlan1`) and RTL8821AU (`wlan2`)
          + | 0bda:881a, 2357:0120 | `rtw88_8812au`, `rtw88_8821au` | 2.4
          + + 5 | **unknown on this kernel** | unknown | no | the in-tree
          + support landed in kernel 6.13 (8812AU) and 6.14 (8821AU) and 
          +the reports describe a **working monitor mode with injection, 
          +without VIF and without active monitor**. This machine runs ke
          +rnel 7.2, so it may just work — the two-radio test (Q8) is the
          + way to find out, and it is the reason no new hardware was ord
          +ered. |                                                       
      447 +                                                              
      448 +The last row matters: **before buying anything, the two-radio 
          +test should be                                                
      449 +run**, because the adapters that are already on the machine ar
          +e driven by an                                                
      450 +in-tree driver that gained monitor mode upstream a while ago, 
          +and this kernel                                               
      451 +is recent enough. The two halves of the test, the script and t
          +he exact                                                      
      452 +capabilities it needs are in §3 and in `QUESTIONS.md` Q8.     
      453 +                                                              
      454 +**Practical notes for the test, if new hardware is needed:** p
          +lug the adapter                                               
      455 +in a **USB 2.0** port (several mt76 adapters lose the monitor 
          +mode and the                                                  
      456 +injection on USB 3), and the in-tree `mt76` drivers need no ou
          +t-of-tree                                                     
      457 +package, no DKMS and no reboot.

      184 +## Q8 — The two-radio RF test: the approval for the privileged
          + action                                                       
      185 +                                                              
      186 +**Status:** **waiting for the approval of the user.** Everythi
          +ng is written                                                 
      187 +and ready; nothing has been run.                              
      188 +                                                              
      189 +**What the test is.** The last unproven step of the primary ob
          +jective: the                                                  
      190 +video stream travelling **over the air** between the two USB r
          +adios, through                                                
      191 +the production receive path, into the desktop player.         
      192 +                                                              
      193 +- **TX:** the TP-Link Archer T2U Plus (USB 2357:0120) sends th
          +e real video                                                  
      194 +  stream, in real RF frames, built by the production TX code  
      195 +  (`radio_build_new_raw_ieee_packet()` + `radio_write_raw_ieee
          +_packet()`,                                                   
      196 +  i.e. a real `pcap_inject()`).                               
      197 +- **RX:** the Eachine WiFiLink (USB 0bda:881a) receives them w
          +ith the                                                       
      198 +  production RX code (`radio_open_interface_for_read()`,      
      199 +  `radio_process_wlan_data_in()`, `packet_process_and_check()`
          +) and hands them                                              
      200 +  over to `process_received_video_component_packet()`, so the 
          +video reaches                                                 
      201 +  the desktop player through the production video pipeline.   
      202 +                                                              
      203 +**What it needs, exactly:**                                   
      204 +- **root** (or `CAP_NET_ADMIN` + `CAP_NET_RAW`): the monitor m
          +ode interfaces                                                
      205 +  and the channel (`CAP_NET_ADMIN`) and the pcap capture / inj
          +ection                                                        
      206 +  (`CAP_NET_RAW`). The application itself is **not** run as ro
          +ot — the desktop                                              
      207 +  player is started as the user of the session.               
      208 +- **a monitor mode interface on each radio**: `iw dev wlan2 in
          +terface add                                                   
      209 +  rubyvtx0 type monitor` and the same for `wlan1`.            
      210 +- **one channel in the 5.8 GHz band** on both (149 by default)
          +. The Eachine                                                 
      211 +  has 5 GHz-only antennas, so the script refuses any 2.4 GHz c
          +hannel and the                                                
      212 +  software guard is not weakened.                             
      213 +                                                              
      214 +**What it changes on the machine, and how it is undone:**     
      215 +- it creates **two new virtual interfaces** (`rubyvtx0`, `ruby
          +vrx0`) on the two                                             
      216 +  USB radios and deletes them at the end (also on an error or 
          +a Ctrl-C);                                                    
      217 +- it sets the channel of the two radios to the 5.8 GHz channel
          + 149 — the                                                    
      218 +  radios are dedicated RubyFPV adapters, they are not associat
          +ed with any                                                   
      219 +  network and they are not the network connection of the machi
          +ne;                                                           
      220 +- it starts the desktop player (as the user) and stops it at t
          +he end;                                                       
      221 +- it does **not** touch `wlan0` (the Intel AX210 that carries 
          +the network                                                   
      222 +  connection): the script identifies the radios by their **USB
          + hardware id**,                                               
      223 +  it refuses `wlan0` by name and it refuses any interface that
          + carries the                                                  
      224 +  default route, and the test program refuses `wlan0` too;    
      225 +- it does not install a driver, does not change a kernel modul
          +e, does not                                                   
      226 +  change any system-wide configuration, does not reboot and do
          +es not touch                                                  
      227 +  the persistent configuration in `~/.config/rubyfpv/`.       
      228 +                                                              
      229 +**How to run it (after the approval):**                       
      230 +```bash                                                       
      231 +cd /mnt/Giochi-e-Altro-2/RubyFPV/RubyFPV                      
      232 +sudo -E ./code/r_tests/two_radio_rf_test.sh 60 149            
      233 +```                                                           
      234 +                                                              
      235 +**What the possible outcomes are, and what each of them means.
          +**                                                            
      236 +1. **The monitor mode works on both radios** (the most likely 
          +outcome: the                                                  
      237 +   in-tree rtw88 driver gained monitor mode upstream in kernel
          + 6.13/6.14 and                                                
      238 +   this machine runs kernel 7.2): the test runs and the video 
          +is received                                                   
      239 +   over the air and displayed. The **RF milestone** is reached
          +, and **no new                                                
      240 +   hardware is needed** — that also answers Q1.               
      241 +2. **The monitor mode does not work on the rtw88 radios**: the
          + script stops                                                 
      242 +   with the exact kernel error and nothing else is changed. Th
          +en the answer to                                              
      243 +   Q1 is that a **monitor-mode-capable adapter is needed**; th
          +e candidates and                                              
      244 +   the evidence are in `STATUS.md` §7 (the recommendation is a
          +n MT7612U or an                                               
      245 +   MT7610U based adapter, e.g. ALFA AWUS036ACM / AWUS036ACHM: 
          +5 GHz, in-tree                                                
      246 +   driver, monitor mode and injection, no DKMS).              
      247 +3. **The monitor mode works but the injection does not**: the 
          +RX side sees the                                              
      248 +   frames of the air but the TX side cannot put them there. Th
          +en the VTX side                                               
      249 +   needs a different adapter, and the RX side is proven.      
      250 +                                                              
      251 +**Decision needed:** the approval to run the privileged two-ra
          +dio test (or to                                               
      252 +skip it, and to go straight to the acquisition of a monitor-mo
          +de-capable                                                    
      253 +adapter).

           +iMaxLength)

           +h);

      343 +                                                              
      344 +   *The capture works.* mac80211 provides the monitor interfac
          +e by itself                                                   
      345 +   (the "software monitor"): `ieee80211_change_interface()` / 
      346 +   `ieee80211_setup_netdev()` call `drv_add_interface()` for a
      347 +   `NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR` interface **only** if the driver a
          +sked for the                                                  
      348 +   active monitor (`MONITOR_FLAG_ACTIVE`) or if it set        
      349 +   `IEEE80211_HW_NO_VIRTUAL_MONITOR`; otherwise the **virtual 
          +monitor**                                                     
      350 +   (`ieee80211_add_virtual_monitor()`) is used, and the driver
          + is never asked                                               
      351 +   to add a monitor vif. The rtw88 drivers set **neither**    
      352 +   `IEEE80211_HW_WANT_MONITOR_VIF` (12), `IEEE80211_HW_NO_VIRT
          +UAL_MONITOR`                                                  
      353 +   (13) nor `IEEE80211_HW_QUEUE_CONTROL` (19) — the flags of t
          +he running                                                    
      354 +   kernel were read from `/sys/kernel/btf/mac80211` — so the v
          +irtual monitor                                                
      355 +   is used and the frames that the driver delivers are copied 
          +to it by                                                      
      356 +   `ieee80211_rx_monitor()`, with the radiotap header that mac
          +80211 builds.

          +type of a                                                     
      358 +   Linux monitor interface is `DLT_IEEE802_11_RADIO` (**127** 
          +in libpcap),

          +ts, and the                                                   
      360 +   production filter (`ether[0x00:2] == 0x0801 && ether[0x0a:4
          +] ==                                                          
      361 +   0x13123456 && ether[0x04:1] == 0x%.2x`) is applied by libpc

      363 +   interface. This was verified twice: with a probe against li

           s the link type

          +face

          +ted as well.

       32 +### 1. What the kernel really does with these two radios (the 
          +settled facts)                                                
       33 +                                                              
       34 +The inherited claim — "the in-tree rtw88 drivers do not implem
          +ent monitor                                                   
       35 +mode" — was **wrong**, and it was wrong in a way that mattered
          +. What was                                                    
       36 +checked, and how:                                             
       37 +                                                              
       38 +| What | Where it was checked | Result |                      
       39 +|---|---|---|                                                 
       40 +| The monitor interface creation | the kernel sources of the r
          +unning kernel (`net/mac80211/iface.c`) | `drv_add_interface()`
          + is called for a `NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR` interface **only** w
          +ith the active monitor or with `IEEE80211_HW_NO_VIRTUAL_MONITO
          +R`; otherwise the **virtual monitor** is used and the driver i
          +s never asked to add a monitor vif |                          
       41 +| The flags of the rtw88 drivers | `/sys/kernel/btf/mac80211` 
          +(the enum of `ieee80211_hw.flags`) | `WANT_MONITOR_VIF` (12), 
          +`NO_VIRTUAL_MONITOR` (13) and `QUEUE_CONTROL` (19) are **not**
          + set → the virtual monitor is used |                          
       42 +| The `MONITOR` case of the driver | the disassembly of the in
          +stalled `rtw88_core.ko` | `rtw_ops_add_interface` handles ifty
          +pe 1 (ADHOC), 2 (STA), 3 (AP), 7 (MESH) and **faults on the ot
          +hers** — but mac80211 never calls it with a monitor, so the `u
          +d2` is never reached |                                        
       43 +| The capture of the frames | `net/mac80211/rx.c` | `ieee80211
          +_rx_monitor()` copies the frames that the driver delivers to t
          +he monitor netdevs, with the radiotap header that mac80211 bui
          +lds |                                                         
       44 +| The link type of a monitor interface | libpcap 1.11 (`gencod
          +e.c`) | `DLT_IEEE802_11_RADIO` = **127**; the production gate 
          +of `code/radio/radiolink.c` accepts it, and libpcap applies th
          +e `ether[...]` offsets **after** the radiotap header, so the p
          +roduction filter matches the real frames |                    
       45 +                                                              
       46 +**Conclusion:** the **capture** of the two rtw88 radios **work
          +s** (the                                                      
       47 +software monitor), and the **injection does not**: an injected
          + frame goes                                                   
       48 +`ieee80211_monitor_start_xmit()` → `ieee80211_xmit()` → `__iee
          +e80211_tx()`,                                                 
       49 +where, without the active monitor and without `WANT_MONITOR_VI
          +F`, there is                                                  
       50 +no vif: mac80211 calls `ieee80211_tx_frags(local, NULL, …)` an
          +d the parallel                                                
       51 +switch in `ieee80211_tx_dequeue()` ends with `info->control.vi
          +f = NULL` — the                                               
       52 +frame is **dropped before it reaches the radio**. `pcap_inject
          +()` still                                                     
       53 +reports a success, so the failure is only visible on the recei
          +ving radio.                                                   
       54 +                                                              
       55 +**Consequence for the mission:** the VRX half of the RF milest
          +one can be run                                                
       56 +with the hardware that is on the machine; the TX half needs an
          + adapter whose                                                
       57 +driver supports the **monitor vif** — the **mt76** family (MT7
          +612U /                                                        
       58 +MT7610U) — or the out-of-tree `rtl8812au` driver (which needs 
          +a new                                                         
       59 +approval: DKMS, a kernel module, a reboot).                   
       60 +                                                              
       61 +### 2. A probe against the real libpcap                       
       62 +                                                              
       63 +A small program (in the temporary directory of the job, not in
          + the repo) wrote                                              
       64 +real radiotap frames in a capture file with the link type 127 
          +and applied the                                               
       65 +**production filter** of `radiolink.c` to them:               
       66 +                                                              
       67 +```                                                           
       68 +A) the production filter, radiotap of 12 bytes:  1 frame read,
          + 1 match                                                      
       69 +B) the production filter, radiotap of 26 bytes:  1 frame read,
          + 1 match                                                      
       70 +C) the single terms of the filter, 26 bytes:     1 frame read,
          + 1 match each                                                 
       71 +D) the single terms of the filter, 12 bytes:     1 frame read,
          + 1 match each                                                 
       72 +E) the same filter with the uplink port byte:    0 frames read
          +, 0 match                                                     
       73 +```                                                           
       74 +                                                              
       75 +The filter matches the frames of a monitor interface whatever 
          +the length of                                                 
       76 +the radiotap header, and it discriminates the port.           
       77 +                                                              
       78 +### 3. A real defect of the production RX path, found and fixe
          +d                                                             
       79 +                                                              
       80 +`code/radio/radiolink.c`: the antenna counter of the radiotap 
          +parsing was                                                   
       81 +**unbounded**, while the arrays that hold the antenna data hav
          +e                                                             
       82 +`MAX_RADIO_ANTENNAS` (4) elements and live on the **stack**. A
          + monitor                                                      
       83 +interface reports **one ANTENNA field per chain**, so a frame 
          +with more                                                     
       84 +chains than the arrays can hold made the code write **outside 
          +of them** —                                                   
       85 +a real memory-safety bug on the path that the RF milestone dep
          +ends on. The                                                  
       86 +counter is now bounded.                                       
       87 +                                                              
       88 +### 4. Test 16: the four exact radiotap layouts of a Linux mon
          +itor interface                                                
       89 +                                                              
       90 +The radiotap header that mac80211 builds is **not** a single f
          +ixed layout: it                                               
       91 +depends on the driver, on the rate and on the number of the ch
          +ains. The                                                     
       92 +previous version of the test used one approximate 32-byte head
          +er. It now                                                    
       93 +builds the **four exact layouts** that mac80211 computes      
       94 +(`ieee80211_rx_radiotap_hdrlen()` + `ieee80211_add_rx_radiotap
          +_header()`):                                                  
       95 +                                                              
       96 +| Layout | Length |                                           
       97 +|---|---|                                                     
       98 +| the legacy rate, without the timestamp of the frame | 18 byt
          +es |                                                          
       99 +| the legacy rate, with the timestamp of the frame | 26 bytes 
          +|                                                             
      100 +| the HT rate (the MCS field), without the timestamp | 21 byte
          +s |                                                           
      101 +| the radiotap namespace (the card reports its chains) | 24 by
          +tes |                                                         
      102 +                                                              
      103 +Each of them is written in a capture file with the link type 1
          +27, read back                                                 
      104 +with the **production RX code** (`radio_open_interface_for_rea
          +d_from_file()`,                                               
      105 +`radio_process_wlan_data_in()`, `packet_process_and_check()`) 
          +and checked:                                                  
      106 +the frames come out **byte for byte identical** to the bytes t
          +hat were on the                                               
      107 +air, every packet passes the **production CRC check**, and the
          + end of the                                                   
      108 +file is reached cleanly.                                      
      109 +                                                              
      110 +### 5. The script: `code/r_tests/two_radio_rf_test.sh`, rewrit
          +ten                                                           
      111 +                                                              
      112 +The script was written before the kernel semantics were settle
          +d and it was                                                  
      113 +wrong in three ways: it created the monitor interface **before
          +** setting the                                                
      114 +channel (so the monitor was born on the 2.4 GHz default channe
          +l of the radio,                                               
      115 +with 5 GHz-only antennas attached), it claimed that the rtw88 
          +drivers have no                                               
      116 +monitor mode, and it started the TX half by default. It now:  
      117 +                                                              
      118 +- identifies the two radios by their **USB hardware id** and r
          +efuses `wlan0`                                                
      119 +  and any interface that carries the default route (the test p
          +rogram refuses                                                
      120 +  `wlan0` too);                                               
      121 +- refuses any channel below 32 (2.4 GHz);                     
      122 +- brings the **managed** interface of the radio **down** (the 
          +kernel refuses                                                
      123 +  to change the channel of a monitor interface while another i
          +nterface of the                                               
      124 +  same radio is up) and **moves the radio to the 5.8 GHz chann
          +el before the                                                 
      125 +  monitor interface is created**;                             
      126 +- **reads the frequency back** after the change and **aborts, 
          +deleting the                                                  
      127 +  monitor, if it is below 5000 MHz** — the Eachine must never 
          +stay on a                                                     
      128 +  2.4 GHz channel;                                            
      129 +- restores the managed interfaces and deletes the monitors in 
          +the cleanup                                                   
      130 +  trap (also on an error or a Ctrl-C);                        
      131 +- runs the **VRX half against the live air** by default (the p
          +roduction                                                     
      132 +  filter is installed on a real monitor interface and the prod
          +uction parsing                                                
      133 +  runs on it) and puts the **TX half behind `--tx`**, printing
          + the reason why                                               
      134 +  the injection cannot work with these adapters, so that the r
          +esult is not                                                  
      135 +  mistaken for a fault of the production code;                
      136 +- checks that the monitor interface really receives the frames
          + of the air                                                   
      137 +  (the RX counters of the interface — `tcpdump` is not install
          +ed on this                                                    
      138 +  machine);                                                   
      139 +- starts the desktop player **as the user of the session** (af
          +ter a                                                         
      140 +  `notify-send`), never as root, and reports precisely what ea
          +ch outcome                                                    
      141 +  means.                                                      
      142 +

      305 +### 2.8 The video retransmission loop, end to end, with the pr
          +oduction code of **both** ends                                
      306 +                                                              
      307 +This is the newest verified result of the port: the **complete
          +** video                                                      
      308 +retransmission loop now runs with the **production code of the
          + vehicle and of                                               
      309 +the station**, and the video of the frame that had a lost pack
          +et reaches the                                                
      310 +desktop player **byte for byte**.                             
      311 +                                                              
      312 +**Why two processes.** The vehicle code and the station code h
          +ave their own                                                 
      313 +copies of the shared variables and their own timers: they cann
          +ot be linked                                                  
      314 +into one binary. The loop therefore runs in two processes, and
          + the **capture                                                
      315 +files stand for the air**: they have the link type of a monito
          +r mode capture                                                
      316 +(`DLT_IEEE802_11_RADIO`, 127), the production filter accepts t
          +hem and the                                                   
      317 +production code parses them, exactly as it does with a live mo
          +nitor                                                         
      318 +interface. Nothing in the loop is a re-implementation of the p
          +rotocol.                                                      
      319 +                                                              
      320 +**The four steps** (`code/r_tests/video_retransmission_loop_te
          +st.sh`, the                                                   
      321 +logs are in `/tmp/ruby/rtr_loop`):                            
      322 +                                                              
      323 +| Step | What runs | Result |                                 
      324 +|---|---|---|                                                 
      325 +| 1. The vehicle sends the video | the real vehicle video TX c
          +ode (`code/r_vehicle/video_tx_buffers.cpp`) builds the video p
          +ackets, the real radio TX code (`radio_build_new_raw_ieee_pack
          +et()` + `radio_write_raw_ieee_packet()`) frames them and write
          +s them to a capture file | 8/8 checks, 30 video packets, all C
          +RC-ok, 0 retransmitted, the first block has its 4 data packets
          + |                                                            
      326 +| 2. The station loses a packet and asks for it | the real rad
          +io RX code reads the capture, **one** video packet is dropped 
          +on the way, the real station code (`ProcessorRxVideo::periodic
          +LoopProcessor()` → `checkAndRequestMissingPackets()`) builds t
          +he request and the real radio TX code puts it on the air | 14/
          +14 checks: the request asks for exactly the lost packet, it ha
          +s a non-zero retransmission id, it is framed on the **UPLINK**
          + port (0x0E) with a good CRC and the bytes on the air are the 
          +bytes of the request |                                        
      327 +| 3. The vehicle answers | the real radio RX code reads the re
          +quest, the real vehicle code (`process_data_tx_video_command()
          +` → `g_pVideoTxBuffers->resendVideoPacket()`) answers it, the 
          +real radio TX code writes the answer | 7/7 checks: the answer 
          +contains the requested packet, marked **retransmitted** and **
          +high priority**, carrying the non-zero retransmission id, and 
          +every packet passes the production CRC check |                
      328 +| 4. The station receives the answer | the real radio RX code 
          +reads the answer, the answer completes the block, the video go
          +es through `process_received_video_component_packet()` → `Proc
          +essorRxVideo` → `VideoRxPacketsBuffer` → `rx_video_output_vide
          +o_data()` → the FIFO of the desktop player | 24/24 checks: **2
          +0960 bytes** of video reach the player and are a **byte-for-by
          +te copy** of the access units of the clip, the access unit tha
          +t had the lost packet is byte-exact, the retransmitted packet 
          +is counted as retransmitted and it is **not** discarded |     
      329 +                                                              
      330 +**The new seam.** `radio_open_interface_for_write_to_file()`  
      331 +(`code/radio/radiolink.c`) opens a radio interface for writing
          + the RF frames                                                
      332 +into a pcap capture file instead of into the air. The frames i
          +t writes are                                                  
      333 +the frames that would have gone on the air: the same radiotap 
          +header, the                                                   
      334 +same 802.11 header, the same CRC, built by the production TX c
          +ode. The                                                      
      335 +existing read seam, `radio_open_interface_for_read_from_file()
          +`, reads them                                                 
      336 +back with the production filter and the production parsing. Th
          +e live                                                        
      337 +interface is **not touched at all** by the file mode.         
      338 +                                                              
      339 +**Two production details that the loop uncovered** (both are t
          +he production                                                 
      340 +behaviour, not test artefacts):                               
      341 +- A **short** video block always gets **1 EC packet**, even at
          + a 0 % EC rate:                                               
      342 +  the short-block adjustment in `code/r_vehicle/video_tx_buffe
          +rs.cpp` computes                                              
      343 +  `ceil(dataPackets * fECRate + 0.001)`, which is 1 for a rate
          + of 0. A lost                                                 
      344 +  data packet of such a block is therefore reconstructed **loc
          +ally**, with the                                              
      345 +  EC packet, and no retransmission is requested. To exercise t
          +he                                                            
      346 +  retransmission the lost packet has to be one of a **full** b
          +lock (4 data                                                  
      347 +  packets, no EC) — block 1, packet 1, the capture frame 5.   
      348 +- The station refuses a retransmission request whose source id
          + is 0 or                                                      
      349 +  `MAX_U32` (`code/r_vehicle/process_radio_in_packets.cpp`), s
          +o the                                                         
      350 +  controller id has to be set on the station side             
      351 +  (`g_uControllerId = 0x87654321`) for the vehicle to accept t
          +he request.                                                   
      352 +                                                              
      353 +**What this is and what it is not.** It proves that the **soft
          +ware** of the                                                 
      354 +two ends fits together: the request, the answer, the block com
          +pletion and the                                               
      355 +delivery of the video to the desktop player, with the producti
          +on code on both                                               
      356 +sides. It does **not** prove anything about the air: the mediu
          +m is a capture                                                
      357 +file, and the RF hop is still missing (§3).                   
      358 +

       20 +## 2026-10-22 — Session 5: the video retransmission loop, end 
          +to end, with the production code of both ends                 
       21 +                                                              
       22 +The goal of this session was the last unproven piece of the **
          +software** side                                               
       23 +of the primary objective: the **video retransmission loop**. U
          +ntil now the                                                  
       24 +station side of the loop was proven (test 14 of `test_video_rx
          +_pipeline`) and                                               
       25 +the vehicle side was only *read* from the sources; the **vehic
          +le's own answer                                               
       26 +code was never executed**. Now the whole loop runs with the pr
          +oduction code                                                 
       27 +of the vehicle **and** of the station, and the video of the fr
          +ame that had a                                                
       28 +lost packet reaches the desktop player **byte for byte**.     
       29 +                                                              
       30 +The RF hop is still missing (it waits for the approval of Q8):
          + the "air"                                                    
       31 +between the two ends is a capture file. Nothing here is claime
          +d as a radio                                                  
       32 +result.                                                       
       33 +                                                              
       34 +### 1. The new seam: the radio TX side to a capture file      
       35 +                                                              
       36 +`code/radio/radiolink.c` had a read seam (`radio_open_interfac
          +e_for_read_from_file()`,                                      
       37 +added in session 3) but no write counterpart: the production T
          +X code could                                                  
       38 +only put frames on a live monitor interface, with `pcap_inject
          +()`.                                                          
       39 +                                                              
       40 +**Added: `radio_open_interface_for_write_to_file(interfaceInde
          +x, captureFileName)`**                                        
       41 +(`code/radio/radiolink.c`, declared in `code/radio/radiolink.h
          +`).                                                           
       42 +                                                              
       43 +- it creates a pcap handle with `pcap_open_dead(DLT_IEEE802_11
          +_RADIO, 65535)`                                               
       44 +  and opens the file with `pcap_dump_open()`;                 
       45 +- it sets the new flag `bTxToFile` of the TX runtime info;    
       46 +- `radio_write_raw_ieee_packet()` was extended: when the inter
          +face is opened                                                
       47 +  for a file, the frame is written with `pcap_dump()` — **the 
          +very bytes that                                               
       48 +  would have gone on the air** — instead of `pcap_inject()`;  
       49 +- `radio_close_interface_for_write()` closes the dump handle a
          +nd the pcap                                                   
       50 +  handle of the file mode and clears the flag.                
       51 +                                                              
       52 +The frames that reach the file are built by the **production**
          + TX code                                                      
       53 +(`radio_build_new_raw_ieee_packet()`: radiotap + 802.11 header
          + + radio                                                      
       54 +packet + CRC), so the file has the same link type and the same
          + bytes as a                                                   
       55 +monitor mode capture of a real link, and the production RX cod
          +e reads it back                                               
       56 +through the production filter and the production parsing.     
       57 +                                                              
       58 +The live interface is **not** touched in this mode: no monitor
          + mode, no                                                     
       59 +channel, no promiscuous mode, no frequency is set. That matter
          +s, because                                                    
       60 +`wlan0` must never be touched and the test runs as a normal us
          +er.                                                           
       61 +                                                              
       62 +### 2. The new vehicle-side test binary: `test_video_tx_resend
          +`                                                             
       63 +                                                              
       64 +`code/r_tests/test_video_tx_resend.cpp` (new) links the **real
          + vehicle                                                      
       65 +modules** (`MODULE_VEHICLE` + `processor_tx_video.o`, `video_t
          +x_buffers.o` is                                               
       66 +inside `processor_tx_video.o`'s module, `process_radio_in_pack

       68 +

       92 +                                                              
       93 +```bash                                                       
       94 +./test_video_rx_pipeline --rtr-loop <vehicle capture> <request
          + capture> <answer capture|-> <lost packet index>              
       95 +```                                                           
       96 +                                                              
       97 +It installs the fake test radio, opens the vehicle capture wit
          +h                                                             
       98 +`radio_open_interface_for_read_from_file()` on the **DOWNLINK*
          +* port                                                        
       99 +(0x0F), reads the frames with `radio_process_wlan_data_in()` a
          +nd                                                            
      100 +`packet_process_and_check()`, drops **one** video packet (the 
          +one whose                                                     
      101 +ordinal is the given index) and hands the rest to             
      102 +`process_received_video_component_packet()`. Then it lets the 
          +production                                                    
      103 +`ProcessorRxVideo::periodicLoopProcessor()` do its work, takes
          + the request                                                  
      104 +from the production high priority queue, checks it field by fi
          +eld (the                                                      
      105 +retransmission id, the stream index, the flags, the count, and
          + the                                                          
      106 +`(blockId, packetIndex)` list, which must contain the lost pac
          +ket), frames it                                               
      107 +on the **UPLINK** port (0x0E) with the production TX code and 
          +writes it to the                                              
      108 +request capture file.                                         
      109 +                                                              
      110 +With an answer capture file, it reads the answer with the prod
          +uction RX                                                     
      111 +code, feeds the packets to the production pipeline and verifie
          +s that the                                                    
      112 +answer completes the block, that the video that reaches the FI
          +FO of the                                                     
      113 +desktop player is a **byte-for-byte copy** of the access units
          + of the clip,                                                 
      114 +that the access unit that had the lost packet is byte-exact, a
          +nd that the                                                   
      115 +retransmitted packet was counted and not discarded.           
      116 +                                                              
      117 +### 4. The orchestration script                               
      118 +                                                              
      119 +`code/r_tests/video_retransmission_loop_test.sh` (new, executa
          +ble) runs the                                                 
      120 +four steps in two processes and checks the exit status of each
          + one:                                                         
      121 +                                                              
      122 +```bash                                                       
      123 +cd /mnt/Giochi-e-Altro-2/RubyFPV/RubyFPV

      127 +                                                              
      128 +**Result: all four steps green, 0 failures.** The logs are in 
      129 +`/tmp/ruby/rtr_loop`.                                         
      130 +                                                              
      131 +```                                                           
      132 +--- 4. The station receives the answer and the video reaches t
          +he player ---                                                 
      133 +    PASS  the station requested the missing video packet      
          +         got=1                                                
      134 +    PASS  the request asks for the lost packet                
          +         got=yes                                              
      135 +    PASS  the bytes on the air are the bytes of the request   
          +          got=yes

          +          got=yes

          +e clip     got=yes                                            
      138 +    The video that reached the player: 20960 bytes (the clip h

          +yer       got=yes

      144 +                                                              
      145 +The 20960 bytes are the first 8 access units of the clip: the 
          +loop delivers                                                 
      146 +the video of the frames that arrive, not the whole clip, and e
          +very delivered                                                
      147 +byte is identical to the source.                              
      148 +                                                              
      149 +### 5. Two production details the loop uncovered              
      150 +                                                              
      151 +- **A short video block always gets 1 EC packet, even at a 0 %
          + EC rate.**                                                   
      152 +  `code/r_vehicle/video_tx_buffers.cpp` computes              
      153 +  `uECPackets = ceil(dataPackets * fECRate + 0.001)` for the s
          +hort-block                                                    
      154 +  adjustment, which is 1 when the rate is 0. A lost data packe
          +t of such a                                                   
      155 +  block is therefore reconstructed **locally**, with the EC pa
          +cket, and no                                                  
      156 +  retransmission is requested. To exercise the retransmission 
          +the lost packet                                               
      157 +  has to be one of a **full** block (4 data packets, no EC): b
          +lock 1, packet                                                
      158 +  1, the capture frame 5. The test drops that one.            
      159 +- **The vehicle refuses a request whose source id is 0 or `MAX
          +_U32`**                                                       
      160 +  (`code/r_vehicle/process_radio_in_packets.cpp`). The station
          +'s                                                            
      161 +  `g_uControllerId` is `MAX_U32` by default, so the mode sets 
          +it to                                                         
      162 +  `0x87654321`, the same id the vehicle side test uses.       
      163 +

      361 +### 2.9 The **sustained** retransmission loop, with the real d
          +esktop player                                                 
      362 +                                                              
      363 +The loop of §2.8 was then repeated **many times in a row**, wi
          +th the **real                                                 
      364 +desktop player** as the reader of the video FIFO (`ruby_player
          +_desktop -p`),                                                
      365 +so the video of every retransmitted frame is **decoded and dis
          +played**, not                                                 
      366 +only counted.                                                 
      367 +                                                              
      368 +- **The new mode**: `test_video_rx_pipeline --rtr-loop-live <v
          +ehicle capture>                                               
      369 +  <request capture> <answer capture> <vehicle binary> <iterati
          +ons>`. The                                                    
      370 +  station runs the **vehicle test binary as a separate process
          +** (the vehicle                                               
      371 +  code and the station code can not be linked in the same bina
          +ry) in every                                                  
      372 +  iteration, so the answer of every request is produced by the
          + **production                                                 
      373 +  vehicle code** (`process_data_tx_video_command()` →         
      374 +  `g_pVideoTxBuffers->resendVideoPacket()`), not by a recorded
          + file.                                                        
      375 +- **The lost packet changes**: in every iteration a **differen
          +t** data packet                                               
      376 +  of the full block is lost (the position 1, 2 and 3 of the bl
          +ock, in turn).                                                
      377 +  The lost packet is found from the headers of the packets the
          +mselves (a                                                    
      378 +  block with 4 data packets and no EC packet), so the test doe
          +s not depend on                                               
      379 +  a hard coded index.                                         
      380 +- **The state is reset between the iterations** with the produ
          +ction reset of                                                
      381 +  the processor (`ProcessorRxVideo::fullResetState()`), so the
          + same capture                                                 
      382 +  file is received again from the start.                      
      383 +- **The watchdog**: the production code writes the video with 
          +a **blocking**                                                
      384 +  write, so a player that does not read the video would block 
          +the test                                                      
      385 +  forever; a `SIGALRM` watchdog ends the test with a clear err
          +or in that                                                    
      386 +  case.                                                       
      387 +- **The new production accessor**: `rx_video_output_get_bytes_
          +to_local_video_player()`                                      
      388 +  (`code/r_station/rx_video_output.h`) returns the number of t
          +he video bytes                                                
      389 +  that were written to the FIFO of the player. It is the numbe
          +r the                                                         
      390 +  **production** code counted, not a number the test made up. 
      391 +                                                              
      392 +**Result on this machine** (`code/r_tests/video_retransmission
          +_live_test.sh                                                 
      393 +10`, the user was warned with a desktop notification before th
          +e screen was                                                  
      394 +taken over):                                                  
      395 +                                                              
      396 +| What | Result |                                             
      397 +|---|---|                                                     
      398 +| the iterations of the sustained loop | **10 of 10** succeede
          +d, 0 failures |                                               
      399 +| the packets that were lost | 10 (a different one in every it
          +eration) |                                                    
      400 +| the requests of the station / the answers of the vehicle | 1
          +0 / 10, all of them with the production code of the two ends |
      401 +| the video that reached the player | **209600 bytes** (20960 
          +bytes per iteration) |                                        
      402 +| the desktop player | "Received the first video stream data",
          + "Detected the video stream format: NV12 1280x720", "**209600 
          +bytes read, 209600 bytes pushed, 80 frames decoded**" (80 = 10
          + iterations × 8 access units) |                               
      403 +| the screen | the screenshot of the player window shows the *
          +*"LOADING CONTENT"** frame of the clip — the same content the 
          +clip has |

  - Result: 38 PASS, 0 FAIL; 20960 bytes of video byte-for-byte identical to the
    clip, the retransmitted packet counted and not discarded.

  - New mode --rtr-loop-live in test_video_rx_pipeline: the station forks the
    vehicle binary every iteration, so every answer comes from the production

      813 +// Finds the index of the phy of a wireless interface.        
      814 +//                                                            
      815 +// The phy of an interface is read from sysfs, because the out
          +put of "iw dev"                                               
      816 +// cannot be parsed reliably. A phy that has more than one int
          +erface (a                                                     
      817 +// managed one and a monitor one, for instance) does not alway
          +s list the                                                    
      818 +// managed one first, so the line that precedes the name of th
          +e interface in                                                
      819 +// the output is not always the "phy#N" header but an unrelate
          +d line ("type",                                               
      820 +// "txpower", ...). When that parse failed, the phy index was 
          +built from the                                                
      821 +// last character of that unrelated line (a number like 53 or 
          +66), the band                                                 
      822 +// detection was then run on a phy that does not exist, the ra
          +dio was recorded                                              
      823 +// with no supported band at all and it became unusable for th
          +e video link.                                                 
      824 +//                                                            
      825 +// Returns 1 and the phy index if the phy was found, 0 if it w
          +as not.                                                       
      826 +int hardware_get_interface_phy_index(const char* szInterface, 
          +int* pPhyIndex)                                               
      827 +{                                                             
      828 +   if ( (NULL == szInterface) || (NULL == pPhyIndex) )        
      829 +      return 0;                                               
      830 +                                                              
      831 +   *pPhyIndex = -1;                                           
      832 +                                                              
      833 +   char szComm[256];                                          
      834 +   char szBuff[1024];                                         
      835 +                                                              
      836 +   // The name of the phy device of the interface: "phy2" for 
          +example.                                                      
      837 +   snprintf(szComm, sizeof(szComm)/sizeof(szComm[0]), "cat /sy
          +s/class/net/%s/phy80211/name 2>/dev/null", szInterface);      
      838 +   szBuff[0] = 0;                                             
      839 +   if ( 1 == hw_execute_bash_command_raw(szComm, szBuff) )    
      840 +   {                                                          
      841 +      removeTrailingNewLines(szBuff);                         
      842 +      removeLeadingWhiteSpace(szBuff);                        
      843 +      int iLen = strlen(szBuff);                              
      844 +      if ( (iLen > 3) && (0 == strncmp(szBuff, "phy", 3)) && i
          +sdigit(szBuff[3]) )                                           
      845 +      {                                                       
      846 +         *pPhyIndex = atoi(&szBuff[3]);                       
      847 +         return 1;                                            
      848 +      }                                                       
      849 +   }                                                          
      850 +                                                              
      851 +   // The fallback: the "iw dev" output, parsed properly. The 
          +phy of an                                                     
      852 +   // interface is the last "phy#N" header that appears before
          + its name.                                                    
      853 +   szBuff[0] = 0;                                             
      854 +   if ( 1 != hw_execute_bash_command_raw("iw dev 2>/dev/null",
          + szBuff) )                                                    
      855 +      return 0;                                               
      856 +                                                              
      857 +   int iPhyIndex = -1;                                        
      858 +   char* pLine = szBuff;                                      
      859 +   while ( NULL != pLine )                                    
      860 +   {                                                          
      861 +      char* pNextLine = strchr(pLine, '\n');                  
      862 +      if ( NULL != pNextLine )                                
      863 +         *pNextLine = 0;                                      
      864 +                                                              
      865 +      char* pText = pLine;                                    
      866 +      while ( (' ' == *pText) || ('\t' == *pText) )           
      867 +         pText++;                                             
      868 +                                                              
      869 +      if ( 0 == strncmp(pText, "phy#", 4) )                   
      870 +      {                                                       
      871 +         iPhyIndex = atoi(&pText[4]);                         
      872 +      }                                                       
      873 +      else if ( 0 == strncmp(pText, "Interface ", 10) )       
      874 +      {                                                       
      875 +         char* pName = pText + 10;                            
      876 +         while ( (' ' == *pName) || ('\t' == *pName) )        
      877 +            pName++;                                          
      878 +         char* pNameEnd = pName + strlen(pName);              
      879 +         while ( (pNameEnd > pName) && ((' ' == pNameEnd[-1]) 
          +|| ('\t' == pNameEnd[-1])) )                                  
      880 +            pNameEnd--;                                       
      881 +         *pNameEnd = 0;                                       
      882 +         if ( 0 == strcmp(pName, szInterface) )               
      883 +         {                                                    
      884 +            *pPhyIndex = iPhyIndex;                           
      885 +            return (iPhyIndex >= 0);                          
      886 +         }                                                    
      887 +      }                                                       
      888 +                                                              
      889 +      if ( NULL == pNextLine )                                
      890 +         break;                                               
      891 +      pLine = pNextLine + 1;                                  
      892 +   }                                                          
      893 +                                                              
      894 +   return 0;                                                  
      895 +}                                                             
      896 +
