      497 +### 2.11 A **defect of the production code**, found by the RF 
          +test and fixed                                                
      498 +                                                              
      499 +The RF test exposed a real bug of the radio enumeration, and t
          +his one is                                                    
      500 +important: it made a radio **unusable**.                      
      501 +                                                              
      502 +**What happened.** The enumeration found the phy of an interfa
          +ce by parsing                                                 
      503 +the output of `iw dev` with `iw dev | grep -B 1 <name>`, that 
          +is, by taking                                                 
      504 +the line that precedes the name of the interface and by buildi
          +ng the index                                                  
      505 +out of its last characters. That works **only when the interfa
          +ce is the                                                     
      506 +first one of its phy**. A radio that has a **monitor interface
          +** as well                                                    
      507 +(the exact configuration the RubyFPV receive path needs) does 
          +not list the                                                  
      508 +managed interface first, so the line that precedes the name is
          + an unrelated                                                 
      509 +one. During the RF test, on the Eachine, the line was `txpower
          + 13.00 dBm`                                                   
      510 +and the index was built out of the `w` of "txpower":          
      511 +                                                              
      512 +```                                                           
      513 +Executing command raw: iw dev | grep -B 1 wlan1               
      514 +Read process output: 37 bytes. Content: [  txpower 13.00 dBm  
      515 +  Interface wlan1]                                            
      516 +phy string: [txpower], length: 7                              
      517 +Executing command raw: iw phy66 info 2>&1                     
      518 +[HW-R] Interface wlan1 supported bands: [N/A]                 
      519 +```                                                           
      520 +                                                              
      521 +The phy **66** does not exist, the channel list could not be r
          +ead, the                                                      
      522 +**band mask of the Eachine was 0** and the radio was recorded 
          +that way. A                                                   
      523 +radio with a band mask of 0 cannot be tuned at all:           
      524 +`hardware_radioindex_supports_frequency()` returns 0 for **eve
          +ry**                                                          
      525 +frequency, so the 5.8 GHz video link is impossible with that r
          +adio. The                                                     
      526 +same defect was already latent for `wlan0` (the AX210 of `wlan
          +1` has a P2P                                                  
      527 +device before it, so its index was 53 — harmless there, becaus
          +e that radio                                                  
      528 +is not a Ruby radio, but the same bug).                       
      529 +                                                              
      530 +**The fix** (`code/base/hardware_radio.c`): the phy of an inte
          +rface is now                                                  
      531 +read from **sysfs**, which is exact and does not depend on the
          + order of the                                                 
      532 +interfaces of the phy:                                        
      533 +                                                              
      534 +```c                                                          
      535 +cat /sys/class/net/<interface>/phy80211/name      ->  "phy2"  
      536 +```                                                           
      537 +                                                              
      538 +with a **correctly parsed** fallback on the `iw dev` output (t
          +he phy of an                                                  
      539 +interface is the last `phy#N` header that appears before its n
          +ame) and a                                                    
      540 +loud error when the phy cannot be found at all. A radio whose 
          +band list                                                     
      541 +cannot be read is now **reported** (`log_softerror_and_alarm`)
          + instead of                                                   
      542 +being silently recorded as a radio with no band.              
      543 +                                                              
      544 +**The new regression test** (`test_radio_capabilities`, 402 ch
          +ecks now): for                                                
      545 +every radio of the running system it resolves the phy again an
          +d it checks                                                   
      546 +that the resolved index is the stored one and that            
      547 +`/sys/class/ieee80211/phy<N>` really exists. This test **fails
          +** with the                                                   
      548 +old code (the index 66 does not exist) and it passes with the 
          +new one.                                                      
      549 +                                                              
      550 +**The stored radio configuration was refreshed** with the corr
          +ected values                                                  
      551 +(`~/.config/rubyfpv/current_radios.cfg` is a *detection cache*
          +: the                                                         
      552 +application deletes and regenerates it at every start, in     
      553 +`code/r_start/ruby_start.cpp`). The corrected detection is now
          +:                                                             
      554 +`wlan0` → phy#1, `wlan1` → phy#2, `wlan2` → phy#5, and all thr
          +ee have the                                                   
      555 +bands "2.4, 5.8 GHz".                                         
      556 +

       86 +- the desktop player (started as the user of the session, neve
          +r as root)                                                    
       87 +  received **nothing**, because there was no video on the air.
       88 +                                                              
       89 +**This is not a proof of RubyFPV video reception.** No compati
          +ble RubyFPV                                                   
       90 +transmitter was on the air; the monitor interface captured arb
          +itrary Wi-Fi                                                  
       91 +frames. What it proves is that the **capture half** of the rad
          +io path works                                                 
       92 +on the real hardware with the production code.                
       93 +                                                              
       94 +### 4. The defect of the production code that the run exposed 
       95 +                                                              
       96 +The log of the run showed the enumeration reading the phy of `
          +wlan1` as                                                     
       97 +**66**:                                                       
       98 +                                                              
       99 +```                                                           
      100 +Executing command raw: iw dev | grep -B 1 wlan1               
      101 +Read process output: 37 bytes. Content: [  txpower 13.00 dBm  
      102 +  Interface wlan1]                                            
      103 +phy string: [txpower], length: 7                              
      104 +```                                                           
      105 +                                                              
      106 +The `iw dev` output was parsed by taking the line **before** t
          +he name of                                                    
      107 +the interface, and that line is not the `phy#N` header when th
          +e radio has                                                   
      108 +more than one interface — which is exactly the case when a **m
          +onitor                                                        
      109 +interface** is on it, the configuration the RubyFPV receive pa
          +th needs. The                                                 
      110 +index was built out of the `w` of "txpower". The phy 66 does n
          +ot exist, the                                                 
      111 +channel list could not be read and **the Eachine was recorded 
          +with a band                                                   
      112 +mask of 0**, which makes a radio unusable (`hardware_radioinde
          +x_supports_                                                   
      113 +frequency()` returns 0 for every frequency).                  
      114 +                                                              
      115 +**Fixed** in `code/base/hardware_radio.c`: the phy is now read
          + from sysfs                                                   
      116 +(`/sys/class/net/<if>/phy80211/name`), with a correctly parsed
          + `iw dev`                                                     
      117 +fallback, and a radio whose band list cannot be read is now re
          +ported                                                        
      118 +instead of being silently recorded with no band.              
      119 +**Regression test added** to `test_radio_capabilities` (402 ch
          +ecks): the                                                    
      120 +phy of every radio is resolved again and it has to be the stor
          +ed one and it                                                 
      121 +has to exist in `/sys/class/ieee80211`. The stored radio confi
          +guration                                                      
      122 +(`~/.config/rubyfpv/current_radios.cfg`, a detection cache tha
          +t the                                                         
      123 +application regenerates at every start) was refreshed with the
          + corrected                                                    
      124 +values: `wlan0` → phy#1, `wlan1` → phy#2, `wlan2` → phy#5.    
      125 +                                                              
      126 +### 5. The TX blocker, settled against the loaded driver and t
          +he running kernel                                             
      127 +                                                              
      128 +The loaded module was decompressed and disassembled:          
      129 +`/usr/lib/modules/7.2.11-1-cachyos/kernel/drivers/net/wireless
          +/realtek/rtw88/rtw88_core.ko.zst`.                            
      130 +In `rtw_ops_add_interface()` only four vif types are handled —
          + **1** (AP),                                                  
      131 +**2** (STA), **3** (ADHOC), **7** (P2P client) — and everythin
          +g else reaches                                                
      132 +an `ud2`. `NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR` is **6**: **the rtw88 drive
          +rs cannot own                                                 
      133 +a monitor vif**, so mac80211 hands the injected frame over wit
          +h a `NULL`                                                    
      134 +vif and the skb is dropped before it reaches the radio. Two ru
          +ntime                                                         
      135 +observations confirm it: the monitor interface was created **w
          +ithout any                                                    
      136 +kernel oops**, and `ip link del` on it answers **EOPNOTSUPP** 
          +(it is the                                                    
      137 +virtual monitor of mac80211).                                 
      138 +                                                              
      139 +**The smallest change that would enable the TX half:** an adap
          +ter whose                                                     
      140 +in-tree driver owns a monitor vif — the **mt76** family (**MT7
          +612U**,                                                       
      141 +ALFA AWUS036ACM, or the cheaper **MT7610U**), which sets      
      142 +`IEEE80211_HW_WANT_MONITOR_VIF` and implements                
      143 +`NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR` in `add_interface`. The out-of-tree  
      144 +`aircrack-ng/rtl8812au` driver would also work but it needs DK
          +MS, a kernel                                                  
      145 +module and a reboot, which the user rejected. The **roles are 
          +not swapped**:                                                
      146 +the TP-Link stays the intended transmitter and the Eachine the
          + intended                                                     
      147 +receiver.

● All work is done. Here is the report.

  What I did

  1. Verified the RF script's safety (all five points), then ran the 
  receive-only test — no --tx:
  sudo -E ./code/r_tests/two_radio_rf_test.sh 60 149

  2. The six separate RX findings (reported separately, as required):

  Finding: Both monitor interfaces created
  Result: Only one — rubyvrx0 on the Eachine. The TX half wasn't requested, so
  wlan2 was left alone
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: The Eachine captured RF frames
  Result: Yes — the interface counter went 2 → 6 during the 60 s (four real air
  frames)
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: The production capture/packet-processing code ran
  Result: Yes — radio_open_interface_for_read() opened the live interface (fd
  3),
  libpcap installed the production filter, FIFO write end open (fd 4), read for
   60 s
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: Frames matched the RubyFPV video protocol
  Result: No — "radio packets: 0, video packets: 0, bad packets: 0, CRC errors:
  0". The four air frames are ordinary Wi-Fi traffic; the production filter
  correctly rejected them
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: Valid video packets reached the reconstruction path
  Result: No — nothing entered the reconstruction, nothing was written to the
  video FIFO
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Finding: The desktop player displayed a live stream
  Result: No — the player (started as the session user, never root) received
  nothing, because there was no video on the air

  This is not proof of RubyFPV video reception. No compatible RubyFPV
  transmitter was on the air; the monitor captured arbitrary Wi-Fi frames. What
  it proves is that the capture half of the radio path works on real hardware
  with the production code.

  3. The exact remaining TX blocker (verified against the loaded driver and the
  running kernel, not just the sources): I disassembled the loaded rtw88_core.ko
  — in rtw_ops_add_interface() only vif types 1 (AP), 2 (STA), 3 (ADHOC), 7
  (P2P client) are handled, everything else hits ud2. NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR is
  6, so the rtw88 drivers cannot own a monitor vif; mac80211 hands the injected
  frame over with a NULL vif and drops it. Confirmed at runtime three ways: the
  monitor interface was created with no kernel oops, ip link del on it answers
  EOPNOTSUPP (it is mac80211's virtual monitor), and the monitor interface
  appears before the managed one in iw dev.

  Smallest change that enables TX: an adapter whose in-tree driver owns a
  monitor vif — mt76 (MT7612U / ALFA AWUS036ACM, or the cheaper MT7610U):
  in-tree mt76x2u, sets IEEE80211_HW_WANT_MONITOR_VIF, implements
  NL80211_IFTYPE_MONITOR in add_interface, injection verified at all MCS levels,
  5.8 GHz, no DKMS/reboot. It would be the third adapter: TP-Link stays the
  intended TX, Eachine the intended RX — no role swap. The DKMS rtl8812au option
  remains rejected per your earlier decision.

  4. A real production defect the run exposed — found and fixed. The log showed
  the enumeration reading the Eachine's phy as 66: iw dev | grep -B 1 wlan1
  returned txpower 13.00 dBm (not phy#2, because the monitor interface is listed
  first), and the index was built from the w of "txpower". The phy 66 doesn't
  exist → the channel list couldn't be read → the Eachine was recorded with a 
  band mask of 0, which makes a radio untunable
  (hardware_radioindex_supports_frequency() returns 0 for every frequency).

      557 +### 2.12 The TX blocker: an out-of-tree driver for the **exist
          +ing** TP-Link (prepared, **not** installed)                   
      558 +                                                              
      559 +The user changed the decision: a **third** adapter is no longe
          +r the default                                                 
      560 +solution. The existing TP-Link Archer T2U Plus (RTL8821AU, USB
          + `2357:0120`)                                                 
      561 +is to be driven by a compatible **out-of-tree** driver, so tha
          +t it can inject                                               
      562 +the RubyFPV frames in monitor mode. The investigation, the por
          +t and the                                                     
      563 +reversible switch are in `code/radio/driver_88xxau/` (the `REA
          +DME.md` there                                                 
      564 +holds the full document); this section is the summary.        
      565 +                                                              
      566 +**The driver.** `https://github.com/aircrack-ng/rtl8812au.git`
          +, branch                                                      
      567 +`v5.6.4.2`, pinned commit `734485506a30d6237c2deaad666a19f8ca5
          +379f2`. The                                                   
      568 +module file is `88XXau.ko`, the USB driver name is `rtl8812au`
          +.                                                             
      569 +                                                              
      570 +**Why this driver and not another one:**                      
      571 +                                                              
      572 +| Requirement of RubyFPV | Evidence in the driver |           
      573 +|---|---|                                                     
      574 +| the TP-Link itself | `os_dep/linux/usb_intf.c:208`: `{USB_DE
          +VICE(0x2357, 0x0120), .driver_info = RTL8821}` — the exact USB
          + id of the adapter is in the device table |                   
      575 +| monitor mode, with the radiotap link type | `Makefile:59` `C
          +ONFIG_WIFI_MONITOR = y`; `os_dep/linux/ioctl_cfg80211.c:4936` 
          +`mon_ndev->type = ARPHRD_IEEE80211_RADIOTAP` (the link type th
          +at the production RX code reads: `DLT_IEEE802_11_RADIO`) |    
      576 +| **the injection** of a radiotap + 802.11 frame, on a monitor
          + interface | `os_dep/linux/xmit_linux.c:547` `rtw_xmit_entry()
          +` → `core/rtw_xmit.c:4401` `rtw_monitor_xmit_entry()`: the rad
          +iotap header is parsed, the 802.11 frame is copied out and inj
          +ected, honouring the `RATE`/`MCS` fields; the monitor netdev h
          +as its own path at `os_dep/linux/ioctl_cfg80211.c:4721` |     
      577 +| the 5.8 GHz band | the module parameter `rtw_monitor_disable
          +_1m` (`os_dep/linux/os_intfs.c:87`): with the default (**0**) 
          +the driver forces every injected frame to **1 Mbps**, and 1 Mb
          +ps does not exist on the 5 GHz channels, so the frame would ne
          +ver reach the air. It has to be loaded with **`rtw_monitor_dis
          +able_1m=1`** |                                                
      578 +                                                              
      579 +The production code does exactly what this driver supports: `i
          +w dev <if> set                                                
      580 +type monitor` (`code/base/hardware_radio.c:2007` and `:2075`),
          + then                                                         
      581 +`pcap_inject()` of a radiotap + 802.11 DATA frame             
      582 +(`code/radio/radiolink.c`, `radio_write_raw_ieee_packet()`; th
          +e headers are                                                 
      583 +at `code/radio/radiolink.c:105` and `:124`).                  
      584 +                                                              
      585 +**A second, independent benefit:** with the in-tree `rtw88_882
          +1au` the                                                      
      586 +TP-Link is **not even recognised** by the project — the string
      587 +`rtw88_8821au` matches none of the patterns of the radio enume
          +ration                                                        
      588 +(`code/base/hardware_radio.c`, the `strstr(pszDriver, …)` test
          +s), so the card                                               
      589 +is recorded as an unsupported radio. With the out-of-tree driv
          +er the uevent                                                 
      590 +reports `DRIVER=rtl8812au`, which the project maps to         
      591 +`RADIO_HW_DRIVER_REALTEK_RTL8812AU`.                          
      592 +                                                              
      593 +**Kernel compatibility (7.2.11-1-cachyos).** The released driv
          +er does **not**

     frequency, tell me and I'll re-run with the right value — the card only
     hears the channel it is tuned to.
  2. What a "real video transmitter" means here: if it is a conventional analog
     FPV VTX, the capture will prove the RF receive path (monitor mode,
     radiotap, libpcap, frames on the wire) but the GCS will show no video,
     because RubyFPV carries video as its own digital packet protocol inside
     802.11 frames, not as analog video. Frames matching the RubyFPV protocol
     will only appear if the transmitter is a RubyFPV-compatible one. I'll
     report which of the two we actually observed.

● The pcap failure is a capability problem, not a mode problem — and it explains
  the earlier "unknown encapsulation" message too (the code logs the same text
  for pcap_activate() failure, then reports the encapsulation of a handle that
  never opened):

  Router: SOFT_ERROR: Error setting [wlan1] to immediate mode: Attempt to create
  packet socket failed - CAP_NET_RAW may be required
  Router: SOFT_ERROR: ERROR: unknown encapsulation on [wlan1]!

  The router runs with CapEff: 0000000000000000 — no capabilities at all — so
  socket(PF_PACKET, SOCK_RAW) is denied. The earlier verified RF test passed
  because it ran the production RX as root.

  Two constraints shape the fix: the project lives on a nosuid fuse mount, so a
  file capability set there is ignored by the kernel; and CAP_NET_ADMIN must not
  be granted, because radio_links_set_monitor_mode() loops over all WiFi radios
  including wlan0 — with that capability the app could switch your network
  adapter to monitor mode.

  That last one mattered: ruby_start cycles wlan0–wlan3 down and up to detect
  the cards. Unprivileged it silently failed; with CAP_NET_ADMIN it would have
  dropped your network at every start. It's now skipped for the connection
  interface.

      652 +### 2.13 The pairing search never progressed: a gate in the de
          +sktop build, and the privileges the radio needs               
      653 +                                                              
      654 +**The symptom (the user):** "when i run search it never comple
          +tes/progresses                                                
      655 +the search". The log of that run repeats, every ~80 ms and for

      660 +                                                              
      661 +**The root cause, found by reading the log and the code.** The
          + search step                                                  
      662 +cannot advance before the router (`ruby_rt_station`) is ready:
          + the router is                                                
      663 +the only producer of `PACKET_TYPE_LOCAL_CONTROLLER_ROUTER_READ
          +Y`, the central                                               
      664 +stores the timestamp in `g_RouterIsReadyTimestamp`, and       
      665 +`MenuSearch::onSearchStep()` returns without advancing while t
          +hat timestamp                                                 
      666 +is 0 (`code/r_central/menu/menu_search.cpp`, substep 2).      
      667 +                                                              
      668 +The router was **never started**, because the desktop build re
          +fuses to start                                                
      669 +it unless there is a **serial** radio. There were two such gat
          +es, both on                                                   
      670 +`hardware_radio_has_serial_radios()` (which counts only the Si
          +K / ELRS serial                                               
      671 +radios, `code/base/hardware_radio.c`):                        
      672 +                                                              
      673 +- `code/r_central/launchers_controller.cpp` → `controller_laun
          +ch_router()`:                                                 
      674 +  *"Desktop build: not starting the controller router process.
          +"* — that is

          +hdog of the

          +s missing.                                                    
      678 +                                                              
      679 +The Eachine is a **Wi-Fi** radio, not a serial radio, so it ne
          +ver counted:                                                  
      680 +the supported USB radio of this machine was invisible to the g
          +ate. The

          +ure of the air,                                               
      682 +without the capture there is no RubyFPV frame, without a frame
          + the search

          +never started.                                                
      684 +

          +s()`                                                          
      686 +(`code/base/hardware_radio.c`), answers the question the gate 
          +was actually

          +t carries the

          + and the frames                                               
      694 +  of the air are captured with libpcap.

      696 +The exclusion of the network interface is not new: `hardware_r
          +adio_is_protected_interface()`                                
      697 +reads the **default route** (`ip -o route show default` → `dev
          + wlan0`) and                                                  
      698 +refuses every configuration operation on it, so `wlan0` is sti
          +ll never                                                      
      699 +touched, whatever the gate says. The predicate is used in the 
          +two places that

      731 +  **nosuid** mount, and the kernel **ignores** the capabilitie
          +s of a file                                                   
      732 +  that is on such a mount, so the binaries are copied there (b
          +trfs, no                                                      
      733 +  nosuid) and the copies are the ones that are executed (`code

      739 +  file capability).                                           
      740 +

          +ding:** the

          +s **with no

       42 +The search step cannot advance before the router is ready: the

          +archStep()`

          + start it

          + on                                                           
       51 +`hardware_radio_has_serial_radios()` (SiK / ELRS only,        
       52 +`code/base/hardware_radio.c`):                                
       53 +

          +d model 7) and                                                
       60 +was already enumerated as a **supported** radio

          +ock: no router                                                
       63 +→ no capture of the air → no RubyFPV frame → nothing to find,

● The search blocker is fixed in the code; one privileged command is left for
  you.

  Root cause of "search never progresses"

  The log loop was MenuSearch::onSearchStep(): waiting for router to be ready...
  — the search can't advance until ruby_rt_station (the router) is up, because
  the router is the only producer of PACKET_TYPE_LOCAL_CONTROLLER_ROUTER_READY.
  The router was never started: the desktop build gated it on
  hardware_radio_has_serial_radios() (SiK/ELRS only), in two places:

  - code/r_central/launchers_controller.cpp:69 → controller_launch_router() —
    logged "Desktop build: not starting the controller router process."
  - code/r_start/ruby_start.cpp → bStationExpected

  The Eachine is a Wi-Fi radio, so it never counted. Measured on this machine
  (program linking the production hardware_radio.c):

    1: wlan1  driver=rtw88_8812au  supported=1 serial=0 protected=0 
  configurable=1 bands=0x0a
    2: wlan0  driver=iwlwifi        supported=0 serial=0 protected=1
  hardware_radio_has_serial_radios() = 0   <- old gate: router never started
  hardware_radio_has_usable_radios() = 1   <- new gate: router starts

  wlan0 is excluded by both (it carries the default route →
  hardware_radio_is_protected_interface()), so it stays untouched.

  What I changed

  - hardware_radio_has_usable_radios() (code/base/hardware_radio.c:2363): counts
    a serial radio or a supported Wi-Fi card that is not the protected
    interface. Used in controller_launch_router() and in ruby_start.cpp.
    controller_launch_rx_telemetry() keeps the serial-only gate (that process
    handles SiK/ELRS telemetry).
  - ruby_start.cpp: the watchdog would now raise a false alarm at every start
    (the router starts on demand, not at boot) — it now alarms only if the
    station was running and stopped.
  - ruby_rt_station.cpp: null-deref of the current model outside search mode (a
    desktop with no vehicle selected) — now refuses to start with a message.
  - run_gcs.sh: warns at startup if the runtime binaries have no capability.
  - Build: make -j24 station ruby_central ruby_start ruby_rt_station → 0 errors.
    Regression suite green (retransmission loop 25 checks, 0 failures;
    test_video_rx_pipeline, test_sik_serial_path, test_radio_capabilities,
    test_menu_rf_profiles, test_config_persistence PASS). git diff --check
    clean.
  - Docs updated: STATUS.md §2.13 (new) + §2.12 corrected (the out-of-tree
    module was compiled for this kernel — vermagic 7.2.11-1-cachyos, alias 
    usb:v2357p0120, rtw_monitor_disable_1m present — but never
    installed/loaded), PROGRESS.md Session 8, QUESTIONS.md Q10 + new Q11.

      814 +// The ground station configures the radio interfaces by runni
          +ng helper                                                     
      815 +// programs (iw, for example). Those helpers are ordinary prog
          +rams, without                                                 
      816 +// file capabilities, so they lose the privileges of this proc
          +ess when they                                                 
      817 +// are executed: the radio interfaces could not be tuned at al
          +l.                                                            
      818 +//                                                            
      819 +// To give them the privileges that this process has, the capa
          +bilities are                                                  
      820 +// raised as ambient: the ambient capabilities are kept when a
          + non privileged                                               
      821 +// program is executed, so the children inherit them.         
      822 +//                                                            
      823 +// A capability can be raised as ambient only if it is in the 
          +permitted set                                                 
      824 +// and in the inheritable set. The file capabilities of this p
          +rogram are                                                    
      825 +// added to the inheritable set by the kernel, so the capabili
          +ties that were                                                
      826 +// installed on this binary can be raised as ambient.         
      827 +void hardware_raise_ambient_capabilities()                    
      828 +{                                                             
      829 +   #if defined(HW_PLATFORM_LINUX_GENERIC)                     
      830 +   u64 uPermitted = 0;                                        
      831 +   u64 uInheritable = 0;                                      
      832 +                                                              
      833 +   FILE* fd = fopen("/proc/self/status", "r");                
      834 +   if ( NULL == fd )                                          
      835 +   {                                                          
      836 +      log_softerror_and_alarm("[Hardware] Could not read /proc
          +/self/status: the helper processes will not inherit the privil
          +eges of this process.");                                      
      837 +      return;                                                 
      838 +   }                                                          
      839 +   char szLine[256];                                          
      840 +   while ( NULL != fgets(szLine, sizeof(szLine)/sizeof(szLine[
          +0]), fd) )                                                    
      841 +   {                                                          
      842 +      if ( 0 == strncmp(szLine, "CapPrm:", 7) )               
      843 +         sscanf(szLine+7, "%llx", (unsigned long long*)&uPermi
          +tted);                                                        
      844 +      if ( 0 == strncmp(szLine, "CapInh:", 7) )               
      845 +         sscanf(szLine+7, "%llx", (unsigned long long*)&uInher
          +itable);                                                      
      846 +   }                                                          
      847 +   fclose(fd);                                                
      848 +                                                              
      849 +   int iRaisedCount = 0;                                      
      850 +   for ( int i=0; i<CAP_LAST_CAP; i++ )                       
      851 +   {                                                          
      852 +      u64 uMask = ((u64)1) << i;                              
      853 +      if ( 0 == (uPermitted & uMask) )                        
      854 +         continue;                                            
      855 +      if ( 0 == (uInheritable & uMask) )                      
      856 +         continue;                                            
      857 +      if ( 0 == prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE, i, 0, 0, 0) )     
      858 +         iRaisedCount++;                                      
      859 +      else                                                    
      860 +         log_softerror_and_alarm("[Hardware] Could not raise t
          +he capability %d as ambient (error: %d). The helper processes

      861 +   }                                                          
      862 +   if ( iRaisedCount > 0 )                                    
      863 +      log_line("[Hardware] %d capabilities raised as ambient: 
          +the helper processes (iw) inherit them.", iRaisedCount);      
      864 +   else                                                       
      865 +      log_line("[Hardware] No capability could be raised as am
          +bient: this process has no privilege to pass to the helper pro
          +cesses.");                                                    
      866 +   #endif

       783 +### 2.14 Four defects of the running ground station, found in
           + the logs of the user's own session, and fixed               
       784 +                                                             
       785 +The user ran the ground station with the Eachine (`wlan1`) at
           +tached, the                                                  
       786 +vehicle's VTX **powered off**, and reported two things: *"its
           + complains that                                              
       787 +there is a firmware mismatch between the vtx and the vrx, but
           + they are both                                               
       788 +supposedly on 11.8"*, and the OSD showed *"Vehicle OTA softwa
           +re update                                                    
       789 +required"*, *"Video protocols have changed. You must update y
           +our vehicle"*,                                               
       790 +with **0 FPS**. The log of that run (`/tmp/ruby/logs/log_syst
           +em.txt`) is the                                              
       791 +evidence of the four defects below. **None of them is a hardw
           +are problem and                                              
       792 +none of them is about the vehicle: the vehicle really is 11.8
           +.**                                                          
       793 +                                                             
       794 +#### 2.14.1 The false "firmware mismatch" — and it was blocki
           +ng the video, not just the message                           
       795 +                                                             
       796 +**The mechanism.** The OSD of the central decides between "sh
           +ow the video" and                                            
       797 +"show the red background with the OTA message" in            
       798 +`_render_video_background()` (`code/r_central/ruby_central.cp
           +p`). It showed the                                           
       799 +video only when the version of the vehicle software was **exa
           +ctly** equal to                                              
       800 +the version of the controller software, and the version of th
           +e controller is                                              
       801 +`11.8` **build 11801** (`code/base/base.h:36-38`).           
       802 +                                                             
       803 +The version of the vehicle comes from two different places:  
       804 +                                                             
       805 +- the **telemetry**, where the version is a single byte with 
           +4 bits for the                                               
       806 +  major and 4 bits for the minor (`rubyVersion`, `code/radio/
           +radiopackets2.h`),                                           
       807 +  so `Model::populateFromVehicleTelemetryData_v6()`          
       808 +  (`code/base/models.cpp:7097`) can only rebuild `11.8` and *
           +*sets the build                                              
       809 +  number to 0** (the log says it: *"set sw version to: 11.8 (
           +b-0)"*);                                                     
       810 +- the **full model settings sync**, which carries the real bu
           +ild number.                                                  
       811 +                                                             
       812 +So the version of the vehicle is `11.8 (b-0)` until the setti
           +ngs sync                                                     
       813 +completes, and `11.8 (b-11801)` afterwards. In the log of the
           + user's session                                              
       814 +both are there, for the same vehicle (VID 2172108829):       
       815 +                                                             
       816 +```                                                          
       817 +199 log lines:  "... VID: 2172108829, ... software: 11.8 (b-0
           +), ..."                                                      
       818 +168 log lines:  "... VID: 2172108829, ... software: 11.8 (b-1
           +1801), ..."                                                  
       819 +```                                                          
       820 +                                                             
       821 +**The complaint was therefore an artefact of the build number
           + being unknown,                                              
       822 +not a mismatch**, and it was *transient* (it disappears after
           + the sync). But                                              
       823 +while the build number is 0 the condition "the versions are e
           +qual" is false,                                              
       824 +so the red background is drawn **and the video is not display
           +ed at all** — the                                            
       825 +message was not cosmetic, it was hiding the picture.         
       826 +                                                             
       827 +**The fix.** A new function `_classify_vehicle_software_versi
           +on()` in                                                     
       828 +`code/r_central/ruby_central.cpp` classifies the version of t
           +he vehicle in                                                
       829 +three cases — *compatible*, *older* (the vehicle must be upda
           +ted) and *newer*                                             
       830 +(the controller must be updated) — and it compares the **majo
           +r and minor**                                                
       831 +when the build number is unknown, against the first vehicle b
           +uild that speaks                                             
       832 +the current video protocol (`MIN_BUILD_FOR_CURRENT_VIDEO_PROT
           +OCOL = 11503`,                                               
       833 +that is 11.5.03). The three OSD texts (the OTA message, the "
           +must update your                                             
       834 +controller" message and the "show the video" path) now follow
           + that                                                        
       835 +classification instead of an exact equality of the whole vers
           +ion word. The                                                
       836 +build number is still used, when it is known, so a vehicle th
           +at really is too                                             
       837 +old is still told to update.                                 
       838 +                                                             
       839 +#### 2.14.2 The radio could not be tuned: the helper program 
           +lost the capability                                          
       840 +                                                             
       841 +The log of the session has **523** lines of                  
       842 +                                                             
       843 +```                                                          
       844 +[HW-R] Unexpected result: [RTNETLINK answers: Operation not p
           +ermitted]                                                    
       845 +```                                                          
       846 +                                                             
       847 +that come from the `iw` helper that the production code runs 
           +to put the card                                              
       848 +in monitor mode and to tune it (`code/base/utils.cpp`,       
       849 +`hw_execute_process("iw dev %s set type monitor …")`).       
       850 +                                                             
       851 +**The root cause is not the installation of the capabilities*
           +*: the file                                                  
       852 +capabilities of the runtime directory are correct (`getcap` p
           +rints                                                        
       853 +`cap_net_admin,cap_net_raw=ep` on the four binaries) and the 
           +process itself                                               
       854 +has them. The problem is that a **child process does not inhe
           +rit the                                                      
       855 +capabilities of its parent**: at `execve()` the *effective* s
           +et of the child                                              
       856 +is empty, and only the capabilities that are in the **inherit
           +able** set and                                               
       857 +that are **raised as ambient** are kept. The `iw` child there
           +fore ran                                                     
       858 +**without** `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and every attempt to configure th
           +e radio failed.                                              
       859 +                                                             
       860 +**The fix.** A new function `hardware_raise_ambient_capabilit
           +ies()`                                                       
       861 +(`code/base/hardware.cpp`) reads `CapPrm` and `CapInh` from  
       862 +`/proc/self/status` and raises, with `prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RA
           +ISE)`, every                                                 
       863 +capability that is in both sets. The kernel adds the permitte
           +d capabilities                                               
       864 +of a file to the inheritable set, so `cap_net_admin` and `cap
           +_net_raw` can be                                             
       865 +raised. It is called at the start of the two processes that c
           +onfigure the                                                 
       866 +radios: `ruby_central` and `ruby_rt_station`                 
       867 +(`code/r_central/ruby_central.cpp`, `code/r_station/ruby_rt_s
           +tation.cpp`).                                                
       868 +The log line of the new code is:                             
       869 +                                                             
       870 +```                                                          
       871 +[Hardware] 2 capabilities raised as ambient: the helper proce
           +sses (iw) inherit them.                                      
       872 +```                                                          
       873 +                                                             
       874 +**No privilege was added and nothing was changed system-wide*
           +*: the process                                               
       875 +keeps the capabilities it already had, it only passes them on
           + to the helper                                               
       876 +it starts.                                                   
       877 +                                                             
       878 +#### 2.14.3 The IPC storm: the router wrote into a channel th
           +at nobody read                                               
       879 +                                                             
       880 +The log of the session has **5600** lines of                 
       881 +                                                             
       882 +```                                                          
       883 +Router: SOFT_ERROR: [IPC] Failed to write to IPC [ROUTER-TO-T
           +ELEMETRY], error code: EAGAIN                                
       884 +Router: [IPC] Channel [ROUTER-TO-TELEMETRY] (fd 262175, uniqu
           +e id 5) info: 84 pending messages, 16300 used bytes, max byte
           +s in the IPC channel: 16384 bytes                            
       885 +Router: SOFT_ERROR: Main loop took too long (max 13 ms, fps: 
           +60): 21 ms                                                   
       886 +```                                                          
       887 +                                                             
       888 +The channel was **full** (16300 of 16384 bytes, 84 messages w
           +aiting) and                                                  
       889 +nothing ever read it: the reader of that channel is `ruby_rx_
           +telemetry`, that                                             
       890 +the desktop **never starts** (it is the process that handles 
           +the telemetry of                                             
       891 +a SiK / ELRS radio; the telemetry of a Wi-Fi link is carried 
           +by the radio                                                 
       892 +link itself). Every write failed, and the retry loop of the I
           +PC write                                                     
       893 +(`msgsnd(..., IPC_NOWAIT)` with 3 attempts and a 10 ms pause 
           +between them)                                                
       894 +**wasted 30 ms per message**: the main loop of the router too
           +k 21 ms instead                                              
       895 +of 13 ms, forever.                                           
       896 +                                                             
       897 +**The fix.** In `open_pipes()` (`code/r_station/ruby_rt_stati
           +on.cpp`) the                                                 
       898 +write endpoint of that channel is opened **only when there is
           + a serial radio**                                            
       899 +(`hardware_radio_has_serial_radios()`); on the desktop there 
           +is none, so the                                              
       900 +router does not write into a channel that nobody reads. The c
           +hannel is still                                              
       901 +there for the case it is made for.                           
       902 +                                                             
       903 +#### 2.14.4 The radio RX thread burned a full core           
       904 +                                                             
       905 +The router's radio RX thread (`code/radio/radio_rx.c`) was at
           + **100 % CPU**                                               
       906 +with the vehicle off, i.e. with **nothing to receive**. The r
           +eason is the                                                 
       907 +poll loop: the thread polls the file descriptor of the captur
           +e and it read                                                
       908 +the packet **only if the poll reported `POLLIN`**. A poll can
           + also report                                                 
       909 +`POLLERR` or `POLLHUP` — the `ENOBUFS` of a full receive buff
           +er, that the                                                 
       910 +kernel keeps pending until a read consumes it — and then **no
           + read was ever                                               
       911 +attempted**: the error was never consumed, the poll returned 
           +immediately at                                               
       912 +every iteration, and the thread spun on the CPU.             
       913 +                                                             
       914 +**The fix** (in `code/radio/radio_rx.c`):                    
       915 +                                                             
       916 +- a read is attempted also when the poll reports `POLLERR` or
           + `POLLHUP`, so                                               
       917 +  that the pending error of the socket is consumed and the po
           +ll blocks again;                                             
       918 +- when a poll wake-up produced **no packet at all**, the thre
           +ad waits 1 ms                                                
       919 +  before polling again, so that no condition can make it spin
           +;                                                            
       920 +- `radio_process_wlan_data_in()` (`code/radio/radiolink.c`) u
           +ses                                                          
       921 +  **`pcap_next_ex()`** instead of `pcap_next()`: the two are 
           +not the same                                                 
       922 +  thing here. `pcap_next()` returns `NULL` both when there is
           + no packet and                                               
       923 +  when the read failed, and the error was **invisible**; `pca
           +p_next_ex()`                                                 
       924 +  distinguishes them (0 = no packet, < 0 = error) and the err
           +or is now logged                                             
       925 +  (every 10th, so that a full buffer does not flood the log).
           + The interface                                               
       926 +  is **not** declared broken on a transient error: only a rea
           +l failure of the                                             
       927 +  interface does that.                                       
       928 +                                                             
       929 +The production RX path is covered by the regression suite: th
           +e retransmission                                             
       930 +loop test reads **all** the frames of the capture through thi
           +s code                                                       
       931 +("all the RF frames of the vehicle were read by the RX code: 
           +30") and the                                                 
       932 +video of the frame that had a lost packet still reaches the p
           +layer byte for                                               
       933 +byte.                                                        
       934 +                                                             
       935 +#### 2.14.5 The router died every ~56 seconds — the watchdog,
           + and what is still open                                      
       936 +                                                             
       937 +The central watches the router (`code/r_central/link_watch.cp
           +p`): if the

       20 +## 2026-10-22 — Session 9: the four defects of the running gro

          +ng below.                                                     
       37 +                                                              
       38 +### 2. The false "firmware mismatch" — and it was hiding the v
          +ideo                                                          
       39 +                                                              
       40 +The OSD decides between "show the video" and "show the red bac
          +kground with                                                  
       41 +the OTA message" in `_render_video_background()`              
       42 +(`code/r_central/ruby_central.cpp`): the video was shown only 
          +when the                                                      
       43 +version of the vehicle was **exactly** equal to the version of
          + the controller                                               
       44 +(`11.8` build `11801`, `code/base/base.h:36-38`).             
       45 +                                                              
       46 +The version of the vehicle comes from two places: the **teleme
          +try**, where it                                               
       47 +is one byte with 4+4 bits (major/minor only — so              
       48 +`Model::populateFromVehicleTelemetryData_v6()`, `code/base/mod
          +els.cpp:7097`,                                                
       49 +can only rebuild `11.8` and **sets the build number to 0**: *"
          +set sw version                                                
       50 +to: 11.8 (b-0)"*), and the **full model settings sync**, which
          + carries the                                                  
       51 +real build number. Both are in the log, for the same vehicle (
          +VID 2172108829):                                              
       52 +                                                              
       53 +```                                                           
       54 +199 lines:  software: 11.8 (b-0)        <- the telemetry, the 
          +build is unknown                                              
       55 +168 lines:  software: 11.8 (b-11801)   <- the truth, after the
          + settings sync                                                
       56 +```                                                           
       57 +                                                              
       58 +So the vehicle really is 11.8 (build 11801 = 11.8.01): the com
          +plaint was an                                                 
       59 +artefact of the unknown build number, and it was **not** cosme
          +tic — while the                                               
       60 +build number is 0 the condition "the versions are equal" is fa
          +lse, so the                                                   
       61 +**video was not displayed at all**.                           
       62 +                                                              
       63 +**The fix.** A new `_classify_vehicle_software_version()` in  
       64 +`code/r_central/ruby_central.cpp` classifies the version of th
          +e vehicle as                                                  
       65 +*compatible* / *older* (the vehicle must be updated) / *newer*
          + (the controller                                              
       66 +must be updated) and compares the **major and minor** when the
          + build number                                                 
       67 +is unknown, against `MIN_BUILD_FOR_CURRENT_VIDEO_PROTOCOL = 11
          +503` (the first                                               
       68 +vehicle build that speaks the current video protocol). All the
          + OSD call sites                                               
       69 +follow that classification. The build number is still used whe
          +n it is known,                                                
       70 +so a vehicle that really is too old is still told to update.  
       71 +                                                              
       72 +### 3. The radio could not be tuned: the helper program lost t
          +he capability                                                 
       73 +                                                              
       74 +The log has **523** lines of                                  
       75 +                                                              
       76 +```                                                           
       77 +[HW-R] Unexpected result: [RTNETLINK answers: Operation not pe
          +rmitted]                                                      
       78 +```                                                           
       79 +                                                              
       80 +from the `iw` helper that the production code runs to put the 
          +card in                                                       
       81 +monitor mode and to tune it.                                  
       82 +                                                              
       83 +**The capabilities were installed correctly** (`getcap` shows 
       84 +`cap_net_admin,cap_net_raw=ep`), and the process itself had th
          +em — but the                                                  
       85 +**child process does not inherit them**: at `execve()` the eff
          +ective set of                                                 
       86 +the child is empty, and only the capabilities that are in the 
          +**inheritable**                                               
       87 +set and that are **raised as ambient** survive. The `iw` child
          + therefore ran                                                
       88 +without `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and every attempt to configure the rad
          +io failed.                                                    
       89 +                                                              
       90 +**The fix.** `hardware_raise_ambient_capabilities()`          
       91 +(`code/base/hardware.cpp`, declared in `code/base/hardware.h`)
          + reads                                                        
       92 +`CapPrm` and `CapInh` from `/proc/self/status` and raises, wit
          +h                                                             
       93 +`prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE)`, every capability that is in bot
          +h sets — the                                                  
       94 +kernel adds the permitted capabilities of a file to the inheri
          +table set, so                                                 
       95 +`cap_net_admin` and `cap_net_raw` can be raised. It is called 
          +at the start of                                               
       96 +`ruby_central` and `ruby_rt_station`, the two processes that c
          +onfigure the                                                  
       97 +radios. **No new privilege, nothing system-wide**: the process
          + passes on                                                    
       98 +what it already has.                                          
       99 +                                                              
      100 +### 4. The IPC storm: the router wrote into a channel that nob
          +ody read                                                      
      101 +                                                              
      102 +**5600** lines of                                             
      103 +                                                              
      104 +```                                                           
      105 +Router: SOFT_ERROR: [IPC] Failed to write to IPC [ROUTER-TO-TE
          +LEMETRY], error code: EAGAIN                                  
      106 +Router: [IPC] Channel [ROUTER-TO-TELEMETRY] ... 84 pending mes
          +sages, 16300 used bytes, max bytes ...: 16384                 
      107 +Router: SOFT_ERROR: Main loop took too long (max 13 ms, fps: 6
          +0): 21 ms                                                     
      108 +```                                                           
      109 +                                                              
      110 +The channel was **full** and nobody read it: its reader is `ru
          +by_rx_telemetry`,                                             
      111 +that the desktop **never starts** (it handles the telemetry of
          + a SiK / ELRS                                                 
      112 +radio; the telemetry of a Wi-Fi link travels on the radio link
          + itself). Every                                               
      113 +write failed, and the retry loop of the IPC write (`msgsnd(...
          +, IPC_NOWAIT)`,                                               
      114 +3 attempts, 10 ms of pause between them) **wasted 30 ms per me
          +ssage**: the                                                  
      115 +main loop of the router took 21 ms instead of 13 ms, forever. 
      116 +                                                              
      117 +**The fix.** In `open_pipes()` (`code/r_station/ruby_rt_statio
          +n.cpp`) the                                                   
      118 +write endpoint of that channel is opened **only when there is 
          +a serial radio**                                              
      119 +(`hardware_radio_has_serial_radios()`); on the desktop there i
          +s none.                                                       
      120 +                                                              
      121 +### 5. The radio RX thread burned a full core                 
      122 +                                                              
      123 +The router's radio RX thread (`code/radio/radio_rx.c`) was at 
          +**100 % CPU**                                                 
      124 +with the vehicle off, i.e. with **nothing to receive**. The th
          +read polled the                                               
      125 +capture descriptor and read the packet **only if the poll repo
          +rted `POLLIN`**.                                              
      126 +A poll can also report `POLLERR` / `POLLHUP` — the `ENOBUFS` o
          +f a full                                                      
      127 +receive buffer, that the kernel keeps pending until a read con
          +sumes it — and                                                
      128 +then **no read was ever attempted**: the error was never consu
          +med, the poll                                                 
      129 +returned immediately at every iteration and the thread spun.  
      130 +                                                              
      131 +**The fix** (`code/radio/radio_rx.c`): a read is attempted als
          +o on                                                          
      132 +`POLLERR`/`POLLHUP`, so the pending error is consumed and the 
          +poll blocks                                                   
      133 +again; when a poll wake-up produced **no packet at all** the t
          +hread waits                                                   
      134 +1 ms, so that no condition can make it spin. In `code/radio/ra
          +diolink.c`,                                                   
      135 +`radio_process_wlan_data_in()` uses **`pcap_next_ex()`** inste
          +ad of                                                         
      136 +`pcap_next()`: `pcap_next()` returns `NULL` both when there is
          + no packet and                                                
      137 +when the read failed, and **the error was invisible**; `pcap_n
          +ext_ex()`                                                     
      138 +distinguishes them (0 = no packet, < 0 = error) and the error 
          +is now logged                                                 
      139 +(every 10th, so a full buffer does not flood the log). A trans
          +ient error does                                               
      140 +**not** declare the interface broken — only a real failure of 
          +the interface                                                 
      141 +does.                                                         
      142 +                                                              
      143 +### 6. The router died every ~56 s — the watchdog, and what is
          + still open                                                   
      144 +                                                              
      145 +The central watches the router (`code/r_central/link_watch.cpp
          +`): if the                                                    
      146 +router does not report for more than 1.1 s, four times in a ro
          +w, the central                                                
      147 +kills it and starts it again. The log has **8** such restarts,
          + one every                                                    
      148 +~56 s:                                                        
      149 +                                                              
      150 +```                                                           
      151 +Central: SOFT_ERROR: Router process is about to fail. Last act
          +ive time: 9283 ms ago, loop counter: 74114                    
      152 +Central: ERROR: Router process has failed. Current router PIDS
          +: [738384].                                                   
      153 +```                                                           
      154 +                                                              
      155 +The last line the router wrote before every death is always th
          +e same:                                                       
      156 +                                                              
      157 +```

      159 +```                                                           
      160 +                                                              
      161 +and then it is silent for **~9.3 s**. The pairing request is t
          +he only thing                                                 
      162 +the router puts on the air while the vehicle is off.          
      163 +                                                              
      164 +**Proved and fixed:** the two proved causes of that silence ar
          +e the EAGAIN                                                  
      165 +storm of §4 (30 ms lost per refused message) and the radio tun
          +ing that could                                                
      166 +not run at all (§3). Both are fixed.                          
      167 +                                                              
      168 +**Not proved:** the exact instruction in which the router bloc
          +ks was **not**                                                
      169 +identified. This machine has `ptrace_scope=1`, so no debugger 
          +can be                                                        
      170 +attached to the running process (`gdb -p` → "ptrace: Operation
          + not                                                          
      171 +permitted", `eu-stack -p` → "Permission denied") and `/proc/<p
          +id>/maps` is                                                  
      172 +not readable either. `pcap_inject()` on the blocking TX handle
          + of a card that                                               
      173 +cannot transmit is the prime suspect, but it is a **suspicion,
          + not a                                                        
      174 +measurement**, and it is not claimed as a fact.               
      175 +                                                              
      176 +### 7. The build of the tree was not reproducible: stale objec
          +t files                                                       
      177 +                                                              
      178 +`test_sik_serial_path` failed with 2 checks (the packet was no
          +t delivered by                                                
      179 +the production RX thread) although it had passed 25/25 the day
          + before. The                                                  
      180 +cause was **not** in the code: the object file of             
      181 +`code/base/hardware_radio_sik.c` was **newer than its source**
          + but had been                                                 
      182 +built from an **intermediate state** of it, in which the file 
          +descriptor of                                                 
      183 +the SiK radio was not stored — the radio was "opened", the wri
          +te worked, and                                                
      184 +the RX thread polled **fd 0** (the standard input) instead of 
          +the serial                                                    
      185 +device. The Makefile has **no header dependency tracking** and
          + cannot see                                                   
      186 +it, so a `make` that looks up to date silently keeps a stale o
          +bject.                                                        
      187 +                                                              
      188 +**The rule that follows:** before a build that has to be **ins
          +talled** and                                                  
      189 +**run**, do `make clean` and build again. After the clean buil
          +d of this                                                     
      190 +session every binary is built from the sources that are in the
          + tree now, and                                                
      191 +the whole suite is green:                                     
      192 +                                                              
      193 +| Test | Result |                                             
      194 +|---|---|                                                     
      195 +| `test_video_rx_pipeline` | 158 / 0 |                        
      196 +| `code/r_tests/video_retransmission_loop_test.sh` | 4 steps, 
          +38 checks, 0 failures |                                       
      197 +| `test_sik_serial_path` | **25 / 0** (it was 23 / 2 with the 
          +stale object) |                                               
      198 +| `test_radio_capabilities` | **399 / 0** |                   
      199 +| `test_menu_rf_profiles` | 43 / 0 |                          
      200 +| `test_config_persistence` | 20 / 0 |                        
      201 +| `git diff --check` | clean |                                
      202 +                                                              
      203 +### 8. What is left for the user                              
      204 +                                                              
      205 +The four fixes are **in the source and built**, but the run di
          +rectory                                                       
      206 +(`~/.local/share/rubyfpv/run`) still holds the **old** binarie
          +s. Copying the                                                
      207 +new ones there (and re-applying the capabilities) overwrites f
          +iles outside                                                  
      208 +the repository and needs the explicit authorization of the use
          +r; until then                                                 
      209 +the fixes are not live and the RF test cannot be run.
